title: Coverage axes
description: What is actually known about a journey catalogue, published as eight SEPARATELY DENOMINATED axes and never as one number. This schema exists to make a single blended coverage figure unrepresentable. The eight axes measure different things against different populations — a journey named in a comment, a journey bound to a test title, a journey a CI step can fail a build on, a journey CI runs but cannot fail on, a journey no CI step touches, a CASE observed passing, a screenshot filed under a journey, a surface a judge looked at — and averaging any two of them destroys the only information they carry. `axes` is closed: adding a ninth property, or any `coverage`/`pct`/`overall` key at the top level, fails validation on purpose.

generated.description: When these figures were measured. Every axis is a measurement with a shelf life; a reader shows this date or it is quoting an unknown.

tool.description: What produced the figures — a script name, or an honest statement that they were assembled by hand. 'Hand-built' is a valid answer and a more useful one than a tool name that did not actually run.

project.description: Optional human name of the system measured.

population.description: The set being measured, and where it came from. Every `of` in `axes` must be drawn from this, so that a reader can tell an axis quoted against the whole catalogue from one quoted against a subset.

flows.description: How many journeys are in scope. This is the denominator for the journey-shaped axes and it must equal the length of `flows` in the flow specification named by `source`.

byPriority.description: The population split by the project's priority vocabulary, so a gate can be quoted against the priority band it actually protects. Keys are the project's own priority values.

byLane.description: The population split by lane, for the same reason.

source.description: The path of the flow specification these figures count against. Without it no axis can be re-derived and none can be trusted.

whyNotReckon.description: When a general reconciliation tool was available and NOT used, the reason. The failure this field prevents is real: a tool's percentages were computed over a different campaign's registry, and publishing them as this campaign's would have been the exact error the tool exists to prevent. Silence here reads as 'the tool's numbers are these numbers'.

axes.description: The eight axes. All eight are required and no ninth is permitted: a project that wants to add a measure adds it to `knownWeak` or publishes a second file, because a new key here would be averaged into the others by the first reader who sees it.

named_any_mention.description: Journeys whose id appears anywhere in a test file, INCLUDING in comment prose. The weakest axis and the one most often mistaken for coverage: a comment mention proves somebody knew the journey existed and nothing else. Publish it only beside `bound_to_a_test_title`, whose shortfall is the size of the lie.

bound_to_a_test_title.description: Journeys whose id appears in a test or describe TITLE, so a specific case is tied to the journey and a runner can report on it by name. This is the join every downstream artefact depends on. Not evidence that the case runs, and not evidence that it asserts anything.

ci_enforced_blocking.description: Journeys bound to a case that a CI step executes AND that can fail the build — the step is required, not report-mode, and its project/flag gate is satisfied. The only axis on which a regression is caught by machinery rather than by somebody looking. Never merge with `report_mode_only`: the difference between them is the whole value of CI.

report_mode_only.description: Journeys CI runs but cannot fail a build on — continue-on-error, an unrequired check, a report artefact nobody gates on. These look identical to enforced journeys in a green dashboard, which is why they get their own count. Promoting one is work, and it is scheduled work, not a formality.

in_no_ci_step.description: Journeys no CI step executes at all, whatever their local status. Publish the priority split here above all others: a high-priority journey in this bucket is the campaign's worst position, since it is named, bound, and completely unwatched.

distinct_recorded_passes.description: CASE ids observed passing in a recorded run. A DIFFERENT POPULATION from the journey axes — one journey can be carried by several cases and one case by several journeys — so this number must be quoted against `ofCases`, never against the journey total, and never subtracted from it.

frames_captured.description: Screenshots that exist and are filed under a journey. Counts pictures, not proof: a frame captured is not a frame anybody looked at, and a frame filed under a journey is not evidence it shows that journey unless the capture recorded what it was pointed at. Carry `flows` beside `n` so the picture-per-journey ratio is visible.

surfaces_judged.description: Surfaces on which a verdict was recorded against a frame — a human or a model actually looked and ruled. Almost always the smallest axis, and the one whose marginal value must be argued rather than assumed; record that argument in `knownWeak`.

isFloor.description: Must be true. Every axis is a lower bound on what is known and an upper bound on nothing: an unnamed journey is not a missing journey, it is an unexamined one. Fixing this to `true` is a refusal to publish these figures as a ceiling.

floorNote.description: Which specific floors are softest, in prose — where a count is inflated by weak inclusion, and where two axes count different populations. Read as a caveat on the numbers above rather than as commentary.

knownWeak.description: Weaknesses the measurement itself found, each with its own count. These are not axes: they are named failure modes inside the axes above, and a reader shows them as deductions rather than folding them in. Keys are the project's own names for the weakness.

blockedNotUnbuilt.description: Journeys or lanes that cannot be measured because of a harness, environment or data problem — NOT because the product lacks the feature. The distinction decides who owns the work, and collapsing it turns an environment fault into a product backlog item. Keys name the blocker; values describe it. An entry recording that a suspected blocker turned out NOT to block is worth keeping, because the belief will recur.

not.$comment: There is no single coverage number. Any of these keys would be read as one, whatever its description said.

axis.description: One axis: a count, the population it is counted against where one exists, and a sentence saying exactly what the count means. `means` is required because every one of these has been misread at least once.

n.description: The count. A raw integer, never a percentage — a percentage hides which denominator it used, and these axes have four different ones.

of.description: The journey denominator, when this axis counts journeys. Omit it rather than borrowing another axis's denominator; an axis that counts something else must use `ofCases` or leave both absent and say why in `means`.

ofCases.description: The CASE denominator, for axes that count cases rather than journeys. Present precisely so that a case count can never be quoted against the journey total.

flows.description: How many distinct journeys this axis's artefacts are spread across, when `n` counts artefacts (frames, verdicts) rather than journeys. Prevents 3,000 screenshots of one screen reading as broad coverage.

byPriority.description: The axis split by the project's priority vocabulary. Required in practice for `in_no_ci_step`, where the high-priority share is the finding.

p0.description: Shorthand for the count in the project's most urgent priority band, when only that band is broken out. Use `byPriority` when more than one band matters.

p0Of.description: The denominator for `p0` — the size of that priority band in the population, not the whole population.

sessionStart.description: What this axis read at the start of the work being reported, so movement is visible and a reader can tell a campaign that ran from one that was already there. It is the only number here that is about the work rather than the product.

p0SessionStart.description: The same baseline for the most urgent priority band.

means.description: One sentence defining the count precisely enough that somebody could reproduce it. Not a label — a definition, including what it deliberately excludes.

instrument.description: The script or command that produced `n`, so it can be re-run. An axis with no named instrument was measured once, by somebody, somehow.

measuredAt.description: When this axis specifically was measured, if it differs from the file's `generated` date. Axes drift apart when a long campaign re-measures some and not others.

note.description: Anything qualifying this axis that `means` should not carry.

weakness.description: A named weakness inside the axes: work that counts toward an axis but should not be trusted by it.

n.description: How many instances. Absent when the weakness is qualitative rather than counted — say so in `status` rather than writing 0.

ofInert.description: A denominator drawn from another weakness, when this one is a subset of it.

sessionStart.description: What this read at the start of the reported work.

status.description: Where a weakness is a claim rather than a count, its standing — `UNPROVEN` is the honest value for a technique whose marginal value has not been demonstrated.

means.description: What the weakness is and why it undermines the axis it sits inside.
